summary: Ten comment-endorsed finds spanning agent workflows, profiling, visual learning, and mechanical clocks.
telegram_footer: 10 items surfaced | 30/30 prior-day front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated

items.name: Gnosis
items.source_story_title: Agents don't need memory, they need documentation
items.summary: Agent decision recorder that captures chosen paths and rejected alternatives after a session.
items.why_included: The creator reports months of successful use with an end-of-session pass.
items.evidence: The creator says Gnosis records decisions and untaken paths, runs a pass at the end, and has worked great for months.

evidence_sources.author: stavros
evidence_sources.excerpt: This just does a pass at the end, rather than consume context all the time. I've been using it for months and it works great.

items.name: Principle Driven Development
items.source_story_title: Agents don't need memory, they need documentation
items.summary: Versioned engineering principles for coding agents; the creator reports strong adherence in practice.
items.why_included: A concrete shared system accompanies a positive two-month first-hand account.
items.evidence: The creator describes versioned principles referenced in code and reports good agent adherence after roughly two months of use.

evidence_sources.author: bushido
evidence_sources.excerpt: System still evolving, but the last two-ish months that I've used it has served me really, really well, And it's been even better with the latest models. I've had surprisingly good adherence from agents on this technique.

items.name: Perfetto
items.summary: Performance trace viewer recommended by a commenter as an excellent modern gpuvis alternative.
items.why_included: A direct recommendation supplies both the alternative and its usable interface.
items.evidence: A commenter says they have found Perfetto an excellent modern alternative to gpuvis.

evidence_sources.author: shadeslayer
evidence_sources.excerpt: I've found perfetto [1] to be a excellent modern alternative to gpuvis.

items.name: Apple Vision framework
items.source_story_title: Show HN: AI search for every photo and every frame of video on macOS
items.summary: Apple's computer-vision framework; a commenter recommends its OCR over Tesseract on macOS.
items.why_included: An explicit platform-specific recommendation identifies a practical OCR alternative.
items.evidence: A commenter recommends Apple's Vision framework for Mac OCR and claims better speed and accuracy than Tesseract; this is not a verified benchmark.

evidence_sources.author: postalcoder
evidence_sources.excerpt: Since this is for the mac you really should be using apple's vision framework for OCR. It smokes tesseract in both speed and accuracy.

items.name: BetterExplained
items.summary: Intuition-first mathematics explanations, strongly recommended in a discussion about how to teach maths.
items.why_included: The comment explicitly recommends the site for building intuition.
items.evidence: A commenter highly recommends BetterExplained as an alternative approach to developing mathematical intuition.

evidence_sources.author: chrisweekly
evidence_sources.excerpt: Regarding intuition, I highly recommend https://betterexplained.com as a great example of an alternative approach that aligns with your ideas.

items.name: Math Made Visual: Creating Images for Understanding Mathematics
items.summary: Alsina and Nelsen's book on understanding mathematics through images and visual reasoning.
items.why_included: The commenter explicitly offers this named book as a useful learning resource.
items.evidence: A commenter suggests Math Made Visual as a resource others might find useful.

evidence_sources.author: rramadass
evidence_sources.excerpt: I recently came to know of the following which others might also find useful; 1) Math Made Visual: Creating Images for Understanding Mathematics by Claudi Alsina and Roger Nelsen

items.name: Mechanical Watch
items.source_story_title: Show HN: Glashütte Trash Clock – A 30-minute pendulum clock made from trash
items.summary: Interactive mechanical-watch explainer by Bartosz Ciechanowski, praised alongside a hands-on clock build.
items.why_included: Explicit affection for the explainer accompanies a direct link and a useful contrasting project.
items.evidence: A commenter links Mechanical Watch and says they love both the explainer and the trash-clock demo for their contrasting approaches.

evidence_sources.author: geerlingguy
evidence_sources.excerpt: (I love both, just opposite in the color vs dryness, jank vs precision, "build first, principles later" approach).

evidence_sources.author: JKCalhoun
evidence_sources.excerpt: The documentary is a fascinating failure and a masterclass in attempting to salvage a show when the whole premise for the show completely collapses.
